description: Pottery is a hands-on clay craft: studio safety, clay bodies and potter’s wheels, designing forms, pottery terms, making hand-built, sculpted and wheel-thrown pieces, firing a kiln, the ceramics industry, and a field experience.

safety.note: Kilns reach extreme temperatures; load and fire them only with a qualified adult, and keep dust down when working with dry clay and glazes.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words.

requirements.title: Safety
requirements.summary: Safety precautions for a potter’s tools, materials and kiln.

requirements.title: Clay and wheels
requirements.summary: What makes a good clay body, and how different kinds of potter’s wheels work.

requirements.title: Designing forms
requirements.summary: Sketching pottery forms, one in a historical style and one of your own design.

requirements.title: Pottery terms
requirements.summary: Terms such as wedging, bisque, slip, stoneware and glaze.

requirements.title: Making pottery
requirements.summary: Hand-built and sculpted pieces, a wheel-thrown piece, and helping fire a kiln.

requirements.title: The ceramics industry
requirements.summary: The ceramics industry and the products it makes beyond craft pottery.

requirements.title: A field experience
requirements.summary: One option: a kiln yard or studio visit, a museum, or researching pottery’s cultural importance.
